items.title: GTA 6 Leak Subpoena: Discord Says It Will 'Evaluate the Validity and Scope Before Responding'
items.description: Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.

On Friday, Andrew L. Carter Jr., Judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, granted Take-Two's request to subpoena Discord to divulge identifying information about users the Rockstar owner believes are tied to the leaks.

Take-Two’s subpoena of Microsoft was also granted. But while Microsoft has issued a statement to say it’s happy to work with Take-Two and Rockstar to help unearth the GTA 6 leaker, Discord issued a different line overnight.

“I can share an update on this,” Discord marketing director Ryan K. Rigney said in a tweet. “Discord has not yet been served with a subpoena from Take-Two. When we do, we'll evaluate the validity and scope before responding.”

Take-Two issued the subpoenas alleging Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) infringement. It wants information and records relating to the ‘CyberLeek’ account, which is allegedly behind the GTA 6 leaks. The subpoenas request identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers. One of the Discord servers mentioned in the filing is 'discord.gg/darkviperau,' which is described as the DarkViperAU editors' server. DarkViperAU is the online name of Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, who has 2.27 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 900,000 followers on Twitch. Judge has denied any wrongdoing.

Reclaim The Net, a group that advocates for free speech and privacy, criticised the Discord subpoena in a tweet.

“Copyright law is supposed to target infringement,” it said. “Here, it’s being used to hunt for identities. Take-Two is seeking DMCA subpoenas that could expose users who didn’t leak or upload GTA VI footage, but who participated in conversations within Discord servers where the leak was discussed."

In an article, Reclaim The Net continued: "One of the Discord servers in question has over 107,000 members, and while it is not clear if Take-Two is going after each and every one of them, the request does say 'all identifying information associated with all user accounts' that were or are members of three named servers since June 1 – and that participated in a conversation in those servers.

"In this case, Take-Two Interactive's one filings make it clear that they're not limited to whoever is uploading the leaks, they're targeting entire communities and channels that are merely existing in the same Discord server as those alleged leakers.

"This is now the pursuit of a membership list under the color of the enforcement of copyright. While it can be crushed if people push back, there's actually nothing about the DMCA process that discourages this in a strong enough way.

"To file a claim is cheap and quick, and the compliance cost falls on the platforms. There was a time when companies would at least try to maintain the guise that their targets were limited to infringement but, these days, they're getting more brazen and now hitting anyone who happens to have been standing nearby."

It is unclear if Microsoft has actually been served with Take-Two’s subpoena, either, although according to court documents it looks like Microsoft had already launched an investigation of its own into the CyberLeek account. Meanwhile, the subpoena for Twitter / X has yet to be signed off, but that may simply be a formality.

All the while, the GTA 6 leaks continue, and there is fresh concern that CyberLeek will release significant story spoilers. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two have issued a statement. IGN has asked for comment.

GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026.

Photo by Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images.

items.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Includes First-Person Sequences — and Yes, Umbrella Is Involved
items.description: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie will pay homage to the series' first-person gameplay, newly-released footage has revealed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie will pay homage to the series' first-person gameplay, newly-released footage has revealed.

A fresh video featuring Cregger discussing his upcoming horror adaptation also includes several quick shots from a first-person perspective, with the barrel of a shotgun and pistol raised directly in front of the camera.

The first moment sees a character — presumably Austin abrams' protagonist Bryan — sneaking through a house with a double-barrelled shotgun raised. The next shot we see is from behind the hands of a character — presumably Bryan again — holding a pistol as a zombie woman leaps towards him, and the camera.

𝙵𝚘𝚛 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚕𝚘𝚟𝚎 𝚘𝚏 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚐𝚊𝚖𝚎.

From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/BHnhoinFS3

— Resident Evil (@ResidentEvil) August 24, 2026

In his commentary, Cregger discusses how his movie will pay homage to how the Resident Evil games typically start players off with a simple pistol, before granting access to a shotgun and later a machine gun. We can see this in the footage shown so far, with the zombie woman seemingly the first undead that Bryan encounters (he hits her on the road) before he takes shelter in a nearby house (and finds a shotgun inside).

And if you're sat there confused as to why first-person is now a thing in Resident Evil, well, the series has evolved a long way since the fixed-camera perspectives of the original Resident Evil 1. Several recent entries have featured a first-person viewpoint, which is also optional in this year's Resident Evil Requiem.

Another behind-the-scenes movie detail has also been released: a document showing the delivery note for Bryan's medical cargo. This is, deliberately, exactly the kind of collectible players find in Resident Evil games, offering a little more detail on what's going on. And indeed, here we see that Bryan's courier charges are being billed to... "Umbrella Corp."

𝚈𝚘𝚞 𝚏𝚘𝚞𝚗𝚍 𝙱𝚛𝚢𝚊𝚗’𝚜 𝚍𝚎𝚕𝚒𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚢 𝚍𝚎𝚝𝚊𝚒𝚕𝚜.

From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/Nv0r96SBzG

— Resident Evil (@ResidentEvil) August 24, 2026

Umbrella was always going to be a part of this movie, as it is set in Raccoon City concurrently with its big zombie outbreak. But how much the company will actually be involved remains to be seen. Cregger has repeatedly made clear that this film will not cross paths with known characters or re-tell story that's already present in Capcom's games.

Indeed, eagle-eyed fans have known for a while this is something of an alternate universe take on Raccoon City's zombie outbreak — which now happens in snow-covered streets and is set in the modern day, meaning characters use smartphones. (Canonically, the city's zombie outbreak happens within the Resident Evil games in September 1998.)

Has Cregger found the right balance between an original story that also pays homage to the source material for existing Resident Evil fans? There's not long left to wait until we find out. Resident Evil arrives in theaters on September 18. Last month, Cregger revealed how the filming of one particular sequence almost killed Austin Abrams when a stunt went slightly wrong.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Baldur's Gate 3: Astarion Excerpt, Narrated by Neil Newbon Himself
items.description: IGN has an exclusive excerpt of Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion, including narration by Astarion actor Neil Newbon himself.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
IGN has an exclusive excerpt of Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion, including narration by Astarion actor Neil Newbon himself.

Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion, from author T. Kingfisher, is a prequel novel set before the events of Larian’s role-playing masterpiece, Baldur’s Gate 3. It follows Astarion during his time in servitude to the vampire lord Cazador Szarr. Stephen Rooney, one of the senior writers of Baldur’s Gate 3, was consulted to help ensure the novel’s authenticity within the game’s world and lore. The audiobook version is narrated by Neil Newbon, and you can see photos of Newbon in the recording booth below.

"This was the one of the very first scenes I wrote, part of getting the geography of the city set firmly into my mind,” T. Kingfisher told IGN. “That was over a year ago and it's hard to believe that the book is so close to coming out. You live with these things in your own head for so long, and I'm delighted that other people will finally get to see it!"

Random House Worlds will publish Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion on September 29, 2026. You can hear Newbon's narration in the video below.

Excerpt from BALDUR’S GATE 3: ASTARION by T. Kingfisher:

In this excerpt, Astarion goes slinking (not skulking) through Baldur’s Gate, seeking fresh blood for his master.

Excerpt:

It was a lovely evening in the Lower City of Baldur’s Gate, which meant that it was foggy but not actually raining, the rats weren’t swarming and nothing untoward with tentacles was coming up from the sea. The ladies, gentlemen, and others of the evening were out in force, the drunks had not yet been turned out of the taverns, and Astarion was slinking through the shadows.

Slinking was a very specific sort of movement, and not to be confused with skulking. Snakes slink, of course, as do cats and cat burglars and most assassins. Thugs and bruisers and most people who break heads for money skulk. (Wolves, interestingly enough, can do either.) The difference is in the fluidity of movement. If you see someone skulking, you wonder who’s going to get their bones broken, whereas if you see someone slinking, you wonder if they’ve got any bones at all.

Astarion slunk past the open door of an inn, where raucous laughter poured into the night. Too busy for his purposes, and too loud. One on the next street was quieter, but he knew for a fact that it was where the Flaming Fists went to drink, and the mercenary troop tended to get very unhappy when their people went missing and had a tendency to turn over rocks to see what was underneath.

As one of the dwellers under metaphorical rocks—albeit a very handsome one, thank you—Astarion was not inclined to stir up trouble.

He kept moving, making a slow circuit past the various inns and taverns. Seven Sins was a tiefling bar, and he’d stand out like an orchid in an abattoir. The Hagstone was perfect—quiet, tastefully appointed, generally full of men hoping to meet other men for conversation and possibly more. It was so perfect, in fact, that he’d taken his last prey from there and figured he should give it a few more tendays before he tried again.

He paused thoughtfully across the street from the Toad’s Ghost, which was holding what appeared to be a poetry night. That might be promising. You could almost always find someone in the back, watching with glazed politeness and absolutely desperate to leave. Of course, the downside was that you also had to listen to poetry. He made a mental note to come back in an hour if nothing else presented itself.

The fog was thickening, muffling the sounds of footsteps and drunken revelry. It barely stirred as he passed. A member of the Watch went by barely an armslength away, but the light of his own lantern reflected off the mist blinded him to Astarion’s presence.

Perhaps I should make use of this fog…

He generally disliked taking people off the street, since inconvenient bystanders had a habit of showing up at just the wrong moment. Not that any bothered to show up for me when I was bleeding to death in an alley, the curs. But with fog this thick, who would ever know?

He turned south toward the docks and continued his slink.

By the time he reached the Sea Tower district and the seedy neighborhood surrounding the docks, the fog was so thick that you could no longer cut it with a knife. You’d need an axe at the very least. The lamps that marked the doorways of taverns shone like lighthouses above the street. Voices echoed strangely off buildings, stretched and distorted, so that it was nearly impossible to tell where the speakers were, or what exactly they were saying.

He paused across the street from Rat’s Run. In many ways, a marvelous place, full of drunken sailors that no one would miss. Perfect for picking up a stranger and luring them back to Cazador’s palace. The owner was a very…interesting…lady who owed him a favor and wasn’t above indicating when she would like someone killed.

He took out his glasses, put them on his nose, and the mist immediately turned them opaque.

“I am foiled at every turn, it seems,” he muttered to himself. The glasses were exceedingly flattering, or so he had been told by numerous people, some of whom had even gone on to live out their natural lifespans. Unable to check in a mirror himself, he had been more than a little worried. The glasses were also host to a very minor illusion, so small and harmless that anyone who sensed it would chalk it up to vanity. Many people wore such charms—necklaces that magically disguised a double chin, earrings that smoothed a pocked complexion, that sort of thing. (In one memorable case, it was underwear that corrected the spelling of a lower back tattoo, a fact which Astarion learned when the underwear came off and he found himself gripping hips marked with the elven characters for “bladder infection.” Fortunately the human man under him had taken his shout of laughter for passion and Astarion had excused himself afterward to go and laugh hysterically in private.)

In Astarion’s case, his glasses turned his eyes blue. It was all well and good to have red eyes when the lights were off, but when he went hunting somewhere well lit, the glasses made life rather easier.

He put the glasses away. The Rat’s Run would be there tomorrow and the next day and probably for the next hundred years after that. Tonight, he would find a victim in the fog.

Astarion made his way along the waterfront, keeping the buildings tightly to his left. The fog was even thicker here, draped over the docks like a funeral shroud, and the last thing he needed was to misjudge a distance and stumble over the wall. The bay here didn’t count as running water but it was cold and full of all sorts of dreadful things. Fish pissed in it. So did sailors. Astarion really did not want to have to squelch home smelling like an estuary.

He passed another spill of light, from a bar, where a halfling was playing an accordion in front of an audience that did not seem to be accordion aficionados. I could probably get more applause by walking in, grabbing that bard by the throat, and dragging them out.

A large piece of dock equipment loomed before him. It looked like a crane, but being nautical, it was probably called a larboard mizzenpoop or something like that. Astarion did not feel the need to clutter up his mind learning names for things on boats. They all sounded like tawdry sex acts, possibly performed with a dead fish.

He leaned against the mizzenpoop for a few moments, letting his eyes adjust to the fog. Small red lanterns gleamed along the street, appearing and disappearing as the breeze off the ocean twisted the fog into strange shapes. Prostitutes, most likely. Hard to do business if the sailors can’t find you.

Astarion did not hunt prostitutes, even though they seemed like they would be easy prey. Not because he was a good man—it was to laugh—but the ladies of negotiable affection watched out for each other, and they would rapidly have noticed that those who went with a certain pale elven client did not come back. Immortality was all well and good, but being tossed into the Chionthar River would mean a short, brutal death by running water.

Petras, who had all the brains of an orange tabaxi, had attempted to hunt prostitutes when he was newly made. Astarion didn’t know what had happened, just that Aurelia had found him in an alley, bloody and shaking and stinking of sewage. It had taken a fair amount of blood to get him healed up and coherent and he wouldn’t talk about it even now.

Truth be told, Astarion had a certain fellow-feeling for prostitutes. The amount of times he’d used his body to lure a victim into Cazador’s clutches probably qualified him for membership in their guild.

As if summoned by the thought, the fog around him flickered red and a voice said, “Hey. You there.”

Astarion swung around and saw a red lantern approaching him, held by a slender figure in clothes that might have been revealing if he could see anything but an outline in the mist. He sighed internally.

“Madam, I’m flattered, but afraid that I’m not looking for company this evening—”

The prostitute came closer, lifting her lantern. “No. I’m looking for you.”

“Me?”

She nodded. She was small and waif-like and Astarion guessed she had at least three knives on her person. “I’ve seen you here before. With your red eyes.”

“They aren’t red,” Astarion said reflexively. “It’s a reflection.”

She stepped close enough that he could see her skeptical expression. Her own eyes were big and brown and could probably look liquid and adoring. At the moment, they looked like frozen agate.

“Ugh. Fine, you’ve caught me. My grandmother was a drow. A dear woman. Had a remarkable way with a snake-headed whip.” Astarion let a faraway look cross his face. “Grandfather always said that’s what attracted him to her in the first place.”

The woman snorted. “Save it for the marks.” Her accent was pure Waterdeep and her ears proclaimed half-elven ancestry. “I’ve seen you before, sometimes with a client. Sometimes a client I know.” She lowered the lantern a little. “Then I don’t see them ever again. Funny, isn’t it?”

Astarion tensed. He could probably overpower her, and no one would notice in the fog, but all the reasons he didn’t hunt prostitutes still held. I could dump her body in the bay. She’d wash up and it would look like she just fell off the dock in the fog. Gods, what a waste of effort, though. All that work and I still wouldn’t have anything to bring back to the old man.

He could practically smell her blood, but he knew better than to dwell on it. Cazador’s proscription was clear. Thou shalt not drink the blood of intelligent beings. Astarion’s victims belonged to the master vampire alone.

He didn’t let any of that show in his voice when he drawled, “You make me sound like a dangerous man, madam. I like it, but wouldn’t that make approaching me…unwise?”

The woman cocked her head. “Three people know I’ve been looking for you. I don’t come back, they know why.”

A chill sank into Astarion’s gut. “And why, exactly, have you been looking for me? Other than my superb good looks.”

“Need your help.”

“My help?” Astarion smiled at her, letting just a little too much canine show. “My help doesn’t come cheap, my darling.”

She gestured over her shoulder with her free hand. “There’s a human named Boris who drinks at the Green Eel. He fancies himself a sailor, but he’s the son of a merchant captain. Won’t have him on the ships anymore. He’s a drunk and a bastard.”

“Sounds delightful.”

The woman’s eyes bored into his, clearly unconcerned about their red sheen. “He doesn’t pay enough to be as rough as he is, and he’s getting rougher. He broken Sheena’s arm last tenday, and the magistrates won’t even hear the case.”

“They wouldn’t,” Astarion said. He wouldn’t have, when he was a magistrate. If a rich brothel owner had brought a suit, that would be another matter entirely, but a street prostitute’s word against a merchant’s son? You’d need a signed eyewitness statement from the head of the Temple of Tyr to even get in the courtroom door. “What do you want me to do about it?”

The woman from Waterdeep smiled beatifically at him. “I want you to make him disappear too.”

He kept moving, making a slow circuit past the various inns and taverns. Seven Sins was a tiefling bar, and he’d stand out like an orchid in an abattoir. The Hagstone was perfect—quiet, tastefully appointed, generally full of men hoping to meet other men for conversation and possibly more. It was so perfect, in fact, that he’d taken his last prey from there and figured he should give it a few more tendays before he tried again.

He paused thoughtfully across the street from the Toad’s Ghost, which was holding what appeared to be a poetry night. That might be promising. You could almost always find someone in the back, watching with glazed politeness and absolutely desperate to leave. Of course, the downside was that you also had to listen to poetry. He made a mental note to come back in an hour if nothing else presented itself.

The fog was thickening, muffling the sounds of footsteps and drunken revelry. It barely stirred as he passed. A member of the Watch went by barely an armslength away, but the light of his own lantern reflected off the mist blinded him to Astarion’s presence.

Perhaps I should make use of this fog…

He generally disliked taking people off the street, since inconvenient bystanders had a habit of showing up at just the wrong moment. Not that any bothered to show up for me when I was bleeding to death in an alley, the curs. But with fog this thick, who would ever know?

He turned south toward the docks and continued his slink.

By the time he reached the Sea Tower district and the seedy neighborhood surrounding the docks, the fog was so thick that you could no longer cut it with a knife. You’d need an axe at the very least. The lamps that marked the doorways of taverns shone like lighthouses above the street. Voices echoed strangely off buildings, stretched and distorted, so that it was nearly impossible to tell where the speakers were, or what exactly they were saying.

He paused across the street from Rat’s Run. In many ways, a marvelous place, full of drunken sailors that no one would miss. Perfect for picking up a stranger and luring them back to Cazador’s palace. The owner was a very…interesting…lady who owed him a favor and wasn’t above indicating when she would like someone killed.

He took out his glasses, put them on his nose, and the mist immediately turned them opaque.

“I am foiled at every turn, it seems,” he muttered to himself. The glasses were exceedingly flattering, or so he had been told by numerous people, some of whom had even gone on to live out their natural lifespans. Unable to check in a mirror himself, he had been more than a little worried. The glasses were also host to a very minor illusion, so small and harmless that anyone who sensed it would chalk it up to vanity. Many people wore such charms—necklaces that magically disguised a double chin, earrings that smoothed a pocked complexion, that sort of thing. (In one memorable case, it was underwear that corrected the spelling of a lower back tattoo, a fact which Astarion learned when the underwear came off and he found himself gripping hips marked with the elven characters for “bladder infection.” Fortunately the human man under him had taken his shout of laughter for passion and Astarion had excused himself afterward to go and laugh hysterically in private.)

In Astarion’s case, his glasses turned his eyes blue. It was all well and good to have red eyes when the lights were off, but when he went hunting somewhere well lit, the glasses made life rather easier.

He put the glasses away. The Rat’s Run would be there tomorrow and the next day and probably for the next hundred years after that. Tonight, he would find a victim in the fog.

Astarion made his way along the waterfront, keeping the buildings tightly to his left. The fog was even thicker here, draped over the docks like a funeral shroud, and the last thing he needed was to misjudge a distance and stumble over the wall. The bay here didn’t count as running water but it was cold and full of all sorts of dreadful things. Fish pissed in it. So did sailors. Astarion really did not want to have to squelch home smelling like an estuary.

He passed another spill of light, from a bar, where a halfling was playing an accordion in front of an audience that did not seem to be accordion aficionados. I could probably get more applause by walking in, grabbing that bard by the throat, and dragging them out.

A large piece of dock equipment loomed before him. It looked like a crane, but being nautical, it was probably called a larboard mizzenpoop or something like that. Astarion did not feel the need to clutter up his mind learning names for things on boats. They all sounded like tawdry sex acts, possibly performed with a dead fish.

He leaned against the mizzenpoop for a few moments, letting his eyes adjust to the fog. Small red lanterns gleamed along the street, appearing and disappearing as the breeze off the ocean twisted the fog into strange shapes. Prostitutes, most likely. Hard to do business if the sailors can’t find you.

Astarion did not hunt prostitutes, even though they seemed like they would be easy prey. Not because he was a good man—it was to laugh—but the ladies of negotiable affection watched out for each other, and they would rapidly have noticed that those who went with a certain pale elven client did not come back. Immortality was all well and good, but being tossed into the Chionthar River would mean a short, brutal death by running water.

Petras, who had all the brains of an orange tabaxi, had attempted to hunt prostitutes when he was newly made. Astarion didn’t know what had happened, just that Aurelia had found him in an alley, bloody and shaking and stinking of sewage. It had taken a fair amount of blood to get him healed up and coherent and he wouldn’t talk about it even now.

Truth be told, Astarion had a certain fellow-feeling for prostitutes. The amount of times he’d used his body to lure a victim into Cazador’s clutches probably qualified him for membership in their guild.

As if summoned by the thought, the fog around him flickered red and a voice said, “Hey. You there.”

Astarion swung around and saw a red lantern approaching him, held by a slender figure in clothes that might have been revealing if he could see anything but an outline in the mist. He sighed internally.

“Madam, I’m flattered, but afraid that I’m not looking for company this evening—”

The prostitute came closer, lifting her lantern. “No. I’m looking for you.”

“Me?”

She nodded. She was small and waif-like and Astarion guessed she had at least three knives on her person. “I’ve seen you here before. With your red eyes.”

“They aren’t red,” Astarion said reflexively. “It’s a reflection.”

She stepped close enough that he could see her skeptical expression. Her own eyes were big and brown and could probably look liquid and adoring. At the moment, they looked like frozen agate.

“Ugh. Fine, you’ve caught me. My grandmother was a drow. A dear woman. Had a remarkable way with a snake-headed whip.” Astarion let a faraway look cross his face. “Grandfather always said that’s what attracted him to her in the first place.”

The woman snorted. “Save it for the marks.” Her accent was pure Waterdeep and her ears proclaimed half-elven ancestry. “I’ve seen you before, sometimes with a client. Sometimes a client I know.” She lowered the lantern a little. “Then I don’t see them ever again. Funny, isn’t it?”

Astarion tensed. He could probably overpower her, and no one would notice in the fog, but all the reasons he didn’t hunt prostitutes still held. I could dump her body in the bay. She’d wash up and it would look like she just fell off the dock in the fog. Gods, what a waste of effort, though. All that work and I still wouldn’t have anything to bring back to the old man.

He could practically smell her blood, but he knew better than to dwell on it. Cazador’s proscription was clear. Thou shalt not drink the blood of intelligent beings. Astarion’s victims belonged to the master vampire alone.

He didn’t let any of that show in his voice when he drawled, “You make me sound like a dangerous man, madam. I like it, but wouldn’t that make approaching me…unwise?”

The woman cocked her head. “Three people know I’ve been looking for you. I don’t come back, they know why.”

A chill sank into Astarion’s gut. “And why, exactly, have you been looking for me? Other than my superb good looks.”

“Need your help.”

“My help?” Astarion smiled at her, letting just a little too much canine show. “My help doesn’t come cheap, my darling.”

She gestured over her shoulder with her free hand. “There’s a human named Boris who drinks at the Green Eel. He fancies himself a sailor, but he’s the son of a merchant captain. Won’t have him on the ships anymore. He’s a drunk and a bastard.”

“Sounds delightful.”

The woman’s eyes bored into his, clearly unconcerned about their red sheen. “He doesn’t pay enough to be as rough as he is, and he’s getting rougher. He broken Sheena’s arm last tenday, and the magistrates won’t even hear the case.”

“They wouldn’t,” Astarion said. He wouldn’t have, when he was a magistrate. If a rich brothel owner had brought a suit, that would be another matter entirely, but a street prostitute’s word against a merchant’s son? You’d need a signed eyewitness statement from the head of the Temple of Tyr to even get in the courtroom door. “What do you want me to do about it?”

The woman from Waterdeep smiled beatifically at him. “I want you to make him disappear too.”

items.title: Pokémon Veteran James Turner Rejoins Franchise Following Work on The Plucky Squire
items.description: Pokémon development veteran James Turner is returning to the world of pocket monsters, after previously leaving to make The Plucky Squire.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pokémon development veteran James Turner is returning to the world of pocket monsters, after previously leaving to make The Plucky Squire.

Turner is notable as being the first Westerner to officially design Pokémon, working for years at the series' core development studio Game Freak. Four years ago, however, Turner departed the company to co-found his own studio, All Possible Futures.

This fledgling team then released innovative indie platformer The Plucky Squire, which saw 2D characters leap from their storybook home to explore 3D surroundings. It's unclear what's next for the studio or any potential sequel now Turner has moved on again.

Last night, Turner revealed via a post on X/Twitter that he had begun a new role as Creative Director of Pokémon Art and Design at The Pokémon Company International. While this doesn't sound like a development role — meaning Turner's days designing species may be over — it will be interesting to see what he does next.

Of course, next year is a landmark moment for Pokémon as the franchise's 10th generation games, Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves, finally arrive for Nintendo Switch 2. Powered by Nintendo's newest console, early footage of the series' next adventures looks hugely ambitious.

Turner designed some of Pokémon's more unusual creatures, such as the ice cream-like Vanillite, colourful fish Bruxish, hulking whale Dondozo, haunted teacup Sinistea, and the sushi-esque Tatsugiri. Other designs he's credited for include the Gene Simmons-inspired Obstagoon, haunted tree Phantump and Ultra Beasts such as the muscled insect Buzzwole and big-jawed Guzzlord.

In the meantime, The Plucky Squire is certainly worth a look if you fancy some clever dimension-hopping platform puzzling. "A beautiful storybook adventure filled with brilliant wordplay-packed puzzles and clever dimension-hopping mechanics," IGN wrote in our The Plucky Squire review, which returned a 7/10, "but it drags on a bit too long after it's already used up all of its best ideas."

Image credit: James Turner.

items.title: Clutch Picks Up a Publisher as Maverick Games Partners with Focus Entertainment
items.description: Focus Entertainment has announced it has forged a “major publishing partnership” with independent racing studio Maverick Games for its upcoming project, Clutch, after Amazon backed out earlier this year.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Focus Entertainment has announced it has forged a “major publishing partnership” with independent racing studio Maverick Games for its upcoming project, Clutch. The company notes the deal “strengthens Focus Entertainment’s portfolio with its first entry into the open-world racing space.”

“At Focus, we look to partner with creators who are redefining their genre,” said Focus deputy CEO Vincent Chataignier in a statement published in conjunction with the announcement. “Mike Brown and his team are regarded as one of the defining creative voices in the racing genre, and Clutch embodies exactly the creative ambition Focus Entertainment wants to champion.”

Clutch is set to arrive on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC early- to mid-2027.

If you missed IGN’s previous coverage of Clutch, it’s a rather glorious-looking racing and driving game that merges circuit racing, street racing, and wild, Fast & Furious-style action and heists. Set in an open-world world inspired by the iconic Mediterranean coastline of the French Riviera, Clutch will feature a map that encompasses Monaco, Cannes, and Saint-Tropez. With a heavy focus on customisation, Clutch will also boast a wild assortment of crazy car-based gadgets to use during its action-based missions, including a grappling hook that can slingshot your car around tight corners.

Founded in 2022 and spearheaded by a number of veterans of Forza Horizon developer Playground Games, Maverick Games had initially partnered with Amazon to publish Clutch. However, Amazon backed out of publishing the project earlier this year, citing the decision was part of a “strategic evolution.”

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past Expansion Confirmed to Include More Gwent, and Everyone Is Already Celebrating
items.description: CD Projekt Red has confirmed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion will come with more Gwent, and card game lovers are already celebrating.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
CD Projekt Red has confirmed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion will come with more Gwent, and card game lovers are already celebrating.

The Witcher 3 earned a lot of praise when it launched back in 2015. While Doug Cockle's gravelly delivery as Geralt helped sell its story, and its RPG gameplay quickly hooked in every kind of fantasy fan, many would say Gwent was what truly kept them coming back for more.

"In Gwent, gamers clash with friends in fast-paced duels that combine skill-based play with bluffing, and careful deck construction," an official description from CD Projekt Red says. "The game is played over a best-of-three series of rounds, as players unleash their hand by slinging spells and diverse units with special abilities, and use clever tricks to deceive their opponents."

CD Projekt Red's in-universe card game first launched within the third installment in its Witcher series before being transformed into a standalone spinoff in 2017 and a real-life tabletop experience in 2025. It's a formula others have unsuccessfully attempted to mimic, but few have managed to stand the test of time quite like Gwent. That's probably exactly why it will be making a comeback when the developer returns to The Witcher 3 with its Songs of the Past expansion in 2027.

CD Projekt Red community and social media manager Marcin Łukaszewski teased the return of the fan-favorite side activity when replying to a player on X/Twitter. When the fan said they hoped more Gwent would be included in the surprise expansion, Łukaszewski offered a simple reply: "Confirmed!"

It's been more than 10 years since The Witcher 3's last expansion, Blood and Wine, came out in 2016, and by the time Songs of the Past launches next year, that wait will have been even longer. CD Projekt Red has teased that this is a full-fledged add-on for the game's story, teasing earlier this year that it will serve as a prologue. In other words, don't expect it to be all Gwent all the time, but for those who have waited to sit down for another round of tabletop challenges, it sounds like there's already more than enough reason to be excited.

pic.twitter.com/o2LfgVq2ih

— Brad (@definitelybrad_) August 23, 2026

Well, I hope whatever the main plot of Songs of the Past is, it’s not urgent.

Because Geralt’s got more Gwenting to do, baby!#Witcher3 https://t.co/IT8PwXY6lZ pic.twitter.com/10vnDoF1gR

— Michał Novigrad (@MichalNovigrad) August 23, 2026

Let's gooooooo!!!!!!!😁⚔️🐺 https://t.co/6xXJ8JoiXt pic.twitter.com/yhylyC1oZw

— Merchant of Novigrad🐺⚔️ (@MofNovigrad) August 23, 2026

IGN called The Witcher 3 "Amazing" in our original 9.3/10 review. We said, "Massive in size, and meticulously detailed, The Witcher 3 ends Geralt's story on a high note." There's plenty more monster hunting to be had as far as CD Projekt Red is concerned, as just earlier today, the studio confirmed The Witcher 4 is on track to launch sometime in 2028.

As for Songs of the Past, we already know that it won't be much longer before we hear more. In fact, news on the expansion is less than 24 hours away, as the developers have already made plans to share more about it during gamescom 2026 Opening Night Live. While we wait to see what's up CD Projekt Red's sleeve, you can read about The Witcher 3 NPCs who just couldn't stop dropping their babies.

items.title: Xbox and PlayStation Appear to Be Publicly Backing Down from Promoting Multiplatform Releases
items.description: Xbox and PlayStation seem to be downplaying their multiplatform presence in new marketing beats.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Xbox and PlayStation seem to be downplaying their multiplatform presence in new marketing beats.

As spotted by PushSquare, Xbox uploaded a new trailer for Minecraft Dungeons 2 on its YouTube channel, which doesn't make any mention of the game coming to PS5 or Nintendo Switch 2. However, the game's previous two trailers, released in March and June respectively, both clearly advertised every platform the title will be released on. It seems like Xbox may be pulling back even further on promoting its games for other platforms now under CEO Asha Sharma.

Earlier this summer, Xbox reportedly pulled the plug on a PS5 version of Gears of War: E-Day just ahead of its reveal. A piece of key art for the game was even shown on an Xbox podcast with a PS5 logo, which was later removed, indicating the decision may have been relatively last-minute. There were also reports that Microsoft pulled a trailer for Halo: Campaign Evolved from a PlayStation State of Play, a move by Sharma that reportedly created tensions between Xbox and PlayStation. It seems like Minecraft Dungeon 2's new trailer may be part of Xbox's strategy to bring players back into its own ecosystem and create brand strength.

Xbox isn't the only one changing its messaging, though. Earlier this year, it was reported that PlayStation is abandoning PC releases for its flashy first-party single-player games like Ghost of Yotei. The company had been releasing the majority of its first-party story-driven games on PC for about half a decade, but it doesn't appear to be part of the strategy going forward. As a result, PlayStation has embraced the "only on PlayStation" branding once again.

In a new PlayStation ad, the words "PlayStation 5 exclusive" are plastered across gameplay for Marvel's Wolverine, Ghost of Yotei, Astro Bot, Gran Turismo 7, Saros, and God of War Laufey. This is meant to signal to players that these games won't be making the jump to PC later and that the company is embracing full-blown exclusivity as it did for decades with the PS1, PS2, PS3, and some of the PS4 generation.

Xbox's strategy still seems a bit wishy-washy, on the other hand. The company has promised permanent exclusivity for Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution, but beyond that, it remains to be seen what will happen. Will The Elder Scrolls 6 be exclusive to Xbox? Will the Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters be exclusive? Only time will tell.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Persona Comes to Beard Papa's With Special 30th Anniversary Collaboration
items.description: Beard Papa’s is teaming up with Persona to celebrate the RPG series’ 30th anniversary with some special cream puffs.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Beard Papa’s is teaming up with Persona to celebrate the RPG series’ 30th anniversary with some special cream puffs.

Beard Papa’s is a Japanese dessert chain with locations sprinkled across the US. It’s best known for its primary offering, cream puffs, which come in a variety of different flavors and combinations for customers to choose from.

Starting September 4, participating Beard Papa’s locations within the United States will transform their interiors and offer up several new flavors of cream puffs in collaboration with Persona.

These storefronts will feature Persona-themed digital menu boards, bakery case graphics, posters, television displays, and more, transforming them into a real-life Persona menu screen. items.title: 'How Do We Get Them to Really Cry at This Scene' — Avengers: Infinity War Director Reveals How They Changed Spider-Man's Death Scene to Break Fans' Hearts
items.description: Avengers: Infinity War director Joe Russo revealed that they changed Spider-Man's death scene on the day it was filmed to try to make audiences cry.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Avengers: Infinity War director Joe Russo revealed that they changed Spider-Man's death scene on the day it was filmed to try to make audiences cry.

When speaking with CBR for a retrospective on Avengers: Infinity War, Joe Russo and Robert Downey Jr. began talking about the impact of the snap at the end of the movie. Half of the heroes crumble into dust, not to be seen again until the end of the next movie, Avengers: Endgame. While most people knew these characters would return, it didn't stop the moment from being emotional in the theater. The death that got fans the hardest is arguably Spider-Man's, which was by design, according to Russo.

"In the script, it was, 'I don't feel so good,' and he goes 'I'm sorry,'" said Russo. "I don't mind a good cry in a movie theater, so I was like, how do we get them to really, really cry at this scene? I brought [Tom Holland] over, and I said, 'You don't want to go. You're 16 years old; it's the last thing you want, is to die.'"

That moment led to Peter Parker essentially pleading to Tony Stark to save him because he was scared to die. Russo went on to note that they knew Spider-Man's death would hit the hardest, so they spent a lot of time developing the relationship between Peter Parker and Tony Stark to make it all the more impactful when it was finally time to kill him off.

"We milked the s**t out of it; it takes the longest of any [of the deaths]. But also the relationship for the movie, writing backwards, is we know if we're going to break your heart, then we should have a fun relationship that's sort of mentor/mentee, but the mentee is a pain in the butt. And you didn't want him to come all along, and you're trying to protect him, and exactly what you didn't want to happen, happens."

Joe Russo will reteam with his directing partner and brother, Anthony Russo, as well as Robert Downey Jr. for Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars. The trailers for Doomsday have teased a bit of what we can expect from their Marvel return, but we'll have to wait and see if it can match the heights of Infinity War and Endgame.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Devs Vow to Update Captain Price After Botched Haircut Goes Viral
items.description: Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after images of his botched haircut went viral.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after images of his botched haircut went viral.

As last weekend's closed beta dredged up conversations revolving around its time-to-kill (TTK) speeds and problematic spawn placements, other fans aimed at Captain Price and his barber. It's mostly thanks to a few images that have circulated across social media, with fans pointing out that, maybe, Modern Warfare 4's version of the classic character should invest in some hair gel.

He looks…unwell, at least when compared to past versions of Captain Price. Whether he's chasing down Vladimir Makarov or walking you through a training course, Price is known to have a full head of hair and a beard that could make even Ghost blush. The one from Modern Warfare 4, however, has neither of those things, and according to many, he hardly looks like the Task Force 141 leader fans have come to know. Activision and Infinity Ward say that's not their intention, but there's also a good reason why only some Call of Duty fans are encountering this choppy imposter.

bro.... https://t.co/JxOTxMTny3 pic.twitter.com/WQEHOTgdEU

— innerghost (@innerghost_) August 23, 2026

that ain't captain Price that's lieutenant Cost https://t.co/gtAFT18NhF

— narancia gaming (@naranciagaming) August 24, 2026

That ain’t price that’s amount

— IPhantom369 (@CJerome369) August 23, 2026

While the Captain Price making the rounds online does appear to be real, he'll only look this way in Modern Warfare 4 if users tune their devices to the lowest possible settings. Some had expected this to be the case, as reports of the botched haircut seemed to mostly be few and far between.

Still, the developers and Activision and Infinity Ward are going to do their best to give the Call of Duty fan-favorite Operator the head of hair he deserves. The studio community teams X/Twitter account replied to a few of the more popular posts, promising it would be addressed "in a future update."

"Captain Price's hair does not appear correctly when viewing his character model at the lowest level of detail," a tab in the "Known Issues" column from the Modern Warfare 4 Trello says.

Hello! We're aware of an issue with Price's hair not appearing correctly when viewed at the lowest level of detail. The team will be addressing it in a future update.

Ultimately this will not be an issue if players meet our recommended specs.

Details: https://t.co/uozRRLS3W5

— CallofDutyCM (@CallofDutyCM) August 24, 2026

What in the 1050 TI is this? Whoever took that screenshot got the game at ultra low, ultra performance, 11% resolution. pic.twitter.com/Pq3A5BdzFt

— The Natty One (@lunatty787) August 23, 2026

What exactly that update entails remains to be seen, but it's far from the only thing on the team's list. Also noted in the Known Issues category are dropped framerates when cooking lethal weapons, hitches for PC players during their first multiplayer matches, a stuck loadout screen bug, and more. TTK is another issue the team is looking into, as are those spawns.

So, if you find yourself dissatisfied with the Modern Warfare 4 beta, you might want to take another crack at it when the open beta launches this weekend. You can learn more about everything it comes with, including its single-player mission, here.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has a release date of October 23, 2026, for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S. For more, you can read about how it will allow players to remove masks for some of its Operators. You can also check out IGN's interview with the team to learn about Infinity Ward's approach to matchmaking, the beta, and more.

Image credit: X user @Runhob.

items.title: Canceled Iron Man Game Footage From Just Cause and Mad Max Developer Leaks Online
items.description: Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.

In the early 2010s, Just Cause and Mad Max developer Avalanche Studios was working on an Iron Man game. The project was never officially announced to the public, but Avalanche Studios co-founder Christofer Sundberg confirmed its development and cancellation during an interview in 2022. Now, gameplay for that title has popped up online via Reddit, reportedly sourced through a PS3 developer kit.

The gameplay is extremely unfinished, but it shows Iron Man flying around in a large environment, fighting jets and attacking various facilities. One of the more in-depth videos appears to be an unfinished E3 demo which shows Iron Man in hand-to-hand combat with soldiers, using a heavy, Arkham-esque style of combat. Of course, he also boasts his repulsors, missiles, and other gadgets to help take down all of his targets.

One of the more standout features is that the environments would've been at least semi-destructible. Iron Man can throw foes through walls, slice them apart in order to make shortcuts for himself, and tear up buildings around him. Beyond that, the build isn't far along enough to really distinguish itself much from SEGA's MCU Iron Man games. It certainly shows promise, though. Given how fun the studio's Mad Max game is and the sandbox gameplay of the Just Cause series, Avalanche probably would've made a killer Iron Man game.

There is still some hope, however. EA Motive is currently developing a new Iron Man game, though details on the project are extremely scarce. The project entered development in 2022, but there haven't been any updates since then. EA was also working on a Black Panther game, which was canceled last year. However, Iron Man has remained in development, despite fears that it will suffer the same fate. Given it has been four years since the announcement, hopefully we are close to hearing some news on the title.

items.title: France and Saudi Arabia to Build $7 Billion Dragon Ball Z Theme Park Outside Paris
items.description: France and Saudi Arabia have come to the mutual conclusion that the world needs Dragon Ball Z theme park. So, they’re building one near Paris to the tune of €6 billion ($7 billion USD).
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
France and Saudi Arabia have come to the mutual conclusion that the world needs Dragon Ball Z theme park. So, they’re building one near Paris to the tune of €6 billion ($7 billion USD).

The Elysee Palace announced the news on Monday, August 23, during the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s visit to Paris. The idea was reportedly first sparked during the Crown Prince’s trip to the city last year, when he and French President Emmanuel Macron discovered their shared love for the iconic anime franchise.

The park will be constructed northwest of the capital city near Cergy-Pontoise, with the massive project expected to create approximately 22,000 jobs. Construction is predicted to take several years, with no opening date publicly announced as yet.

To no one’s surprise, Qiddiya is providing the funds for the project, which will be one of two Dragon Ball Z theme parks once all is said and done. The first theme park was officially revealed on the official Dragon Ball website back in 2024, along with extensive concept art and teasers for what it’ll look like when construction is complete.

The first park is currently being built in Qiddiya City, a massive entertainment hub currently in development just outside the capital of Riyadh. It will reportedly span more than 500,000 square meters, featuring seven recreations of locales from the series including the Kame House, Capsule Corporation, and Beerus's Planet.

Five rides will also be included as part of a 30+ attraction total, along with a 70-meter-tall statue of Shenron. It’s a massive undertaking, and one that isn’t expected to open anytime soon, with no official opening date released at the time of writing.

The announcement of Paris’s Dragon Ball theme park comes after the Esports World Cup was relocated to the city due to security concerns near Riyadh, where it was previously scheduled to take place. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince was in attendance for the competition’s closing ceremony, where Macron was also present.

This is one of several expansive investments the country has made into cultural projects within the gaming and anime space; most recently, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund completed a $55 billion acquisition of EA as part of an investor group alongside Silver Lake and Affinity Partners.

In March, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman's Electronic Gaming Development Company (EGDC) acquired a 5% stake in Capcom, upping its ownership in the famed Japanese game developer and publisher to 10%.

And back in February, Saudi-owned RTS took full ownership of Evo, the world’s largest fighting game tournament series, which has since expanded to include several other global Evo events in a controversial turn of events within the fighting game community.

items.title: Amazon and Twitch Face Class-Action Lawsuit After Introducing Opt-Out Setting That Uses Streamers' Content to Train AI
items.description: Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they opt out.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they manually opt out.

The setting sparked a wave of backlash when it was rolled out last week. "Allow your channel content to train generative AI content models at Amazon," it reads.

It’s buried in users’ security and privacy settings, and is automatically turned on by default. Streamers must toggle the option off in order to opt out of it — but that doesn’t stop Twitch from using their channel content for other purposes, as outlined in the platform’s Privacy Notice.

We've added a setting that lets you opt out of having your channel content used to train generative AI content models across Amazon.

Click here to learn more:https://t.co/C3G0Jt6m0D

— Twitch Support (@TwitchSupport) August 12, 2026

Just a week later, Amazon and Twitch were officially named in a class-action lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on August 20, 2026. In the 37-page complaint, plaintiff Warren Pandiscia — a Twitch streamer based in Connecticut with over 900 followers — argues that Amazon “unlawfully” scraped creators’ content without their consent by automatically opting them into the AI training setting.

“Defendants’ actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation," the suit reads.

"Content creators such as Plaintiff and the Class Members will never be able to claw back the intellectual property unlawfully copied and used by Defendants to train Amazon’s generative AI. Once AI ingests content, that content is stored in its neural network, and not capable of deletion or retraction. Defendants’ actions constitute abuse and exploitation of content creators’ work for Defendants’ profit."

Damages sought include “all available contract damages, including actual, compensatory, consequential, and nominal damages, together with such other relief as the Court deems just and proper,” though no specific monetary amount was mentioned.

Twitch, for its part, has defended its stance on automatically opting creators into Amazon’s AI training. During a ‘Patch Notes’ stream that was broadcast that same day, Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton responded to questions about the setting, saying plainly: “If it was opt-in, nobody would opt in. That’s honestly the answer.”

Twitch’s Account Settings FAQ explains that it trains Amazon’s generative AI on users’ content for things like “[refining] models that create speech to text, which would help improve captions at Twitch but would also help improve captions across Amazon,” and “AI-supported features, like captions, which automatically generate captions for your Clips but does not retain your stream or your clips to train a model that can generate new content.”

Twitch has not provided an official comment on the lawsuit at the time of writing. IGN has reached out for comment.

It’s buried in users’ security and privacy settings, and is automatically turned on by default. Streamers must toggle the option off in order to opt out of it — but that doesn’t stop Twitch from using their channel content for other purposes, as outlined in the platform’s Privacy Notice.

We've added a setting that lets you opt out of having your channel content used to train generative AI content models across Amazon.

Click here to learn more:https://t.co/C3G0Jt6m0D

— Twitch Support (@TwitchSupport) August 12, 2026

Just a week later, Amazon and Twitch were officially named in a class-action lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on August 20, 2026. In the 37-page complaint, plaintiff Warren Pandiscia — a Twitch streamer based in Connecticut with over 900 followers — argues that Amazon “unlawfully” scraped creators’ content without their consent by automatically opting them into the AI training setting.

“Defendants’ actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation," the suit reads.

"Content creators such as Plaintiff and the Class Members will never be able to claw back the intellectual property unlawfully copied and used by Defendants to train Amazon’s generative AI. Once AI ingests content, that content is stored in its neural network, and not capable of deletion or retraction. Defendants’ actions constitute abuse and exploitation of content creators’ work for Defendants’ profit."

Damages sought include “all available contract damages, including actual, compensatory, consequential, and nominal damages, together with such other relief as the Court deems just and proper,” though no specific monetary amount was mentioned.

Twitch, for its part, has defended its stance on automatically opting creators into Amazon’s AI training. During a ‘Patch Notes’ stream that was broadcast that same day, Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton responded to questions about the setting, saying plainly: “If it was opt-in, nobody would opt in. That’s honestly the answer.”

Twitch’s Account Settings FAQ explains that it trains Amazon’s generative AI on users’ content for things like “[refining] models that create speech to text, which would help improve captions at Twitch but would also help improve captions across Amazon,” and “AI-supported features, like captions, which automatically generate captions for your Clips but does not retain your stream or your clips to train a model that can generate new content.”

items.title: Lanterns Episode 3 Teaser Reveals First Look at Hal Jordan Wearing Iconic Green Lantern Domino Mask
items.description: HBO has published the first teaser for Lanterns Episode 3, and it comes with a first look at Hal Jordan wearing Green Lantern's iconic domino mask.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
HBO has published the first teaser for Lanterns Episode 3, and it comes with a first look at Hal Jordan wearing Green Lantern's iconic domino mask.

The network dropped the latest trailer for its DCU show following the conclusion of Episode 2 last night. If you didn't catch it after the credits rolled, the full 42-second Lanterns teaser can now be found on the HBO Max YouTube channel.

Don't worry; it doesn't give away too much. As has already been teased, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) is being set up to be a special part of the DCU as episodes roll out. That means confronting what seems to be a Guardian (played by Laura Linney) and reckoning with his past. If the Lanterns Episode 3 teaser is anything to go by, the Green Lantern-in-training seems to be the star of next week's episode, but the moment that has everyone talking online actually concerns a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment featuring Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler).

John Stewart was born for this.

Watch new episodes of #Lanterns on Sundays at 9pm on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/9SMnO7rINT

— HBO Max (@hbomax) August 24, 2026

Just after the 17-second mark, you can see a few frames from an old TV playing what seems to be footage of the news covering Hal Jordan. He appears to be suited up in the same outfit we've seen Chandler wear in the show itself, but the main difference here is his bright-green domino mask.

So far, Chandler has given DC fans a slightly grumpier version of the Green Lantern they might be used to. While he's generally been hailed as a fitting inclusion for the DCU, connecting his character to the one we've seen featured in comic books and animated projects for decades has been a bit difficult for some. Seeing him suited up in full Green Lantern Corps attire seems to have already helped connect those dots for those fans online.

Warning! Spoilers for Lanterns Season 1 Episodes 1 and 2 follow.

All of that said, this may be a little more than an Easter Egg rather than a sneak peek at what this particular costume will eventually look like in motion. For starters, the end of Episode 1 pretty heavily implied that Hal Jordan's days in the DCU are already numbered. The Episode 3 teaser also suggested that we'll be skipping around the timeline yet again, potentially traveling back to 1996. If we do see Hal Jordan sporting his domino mask, those moments may be limited to a few flashback sequences.

New look at Hal Jordan wearing a domino mask in 'LANTERNS'. pic.twitter.com/d20PWHm6II

— DC Film News (@DCFilmNews) August 24, 2026

MASKED HAL JORDAN YOOOOO #Lanterns pic.twitter.com/R61q87Psp2

— Axel🦇 (@AxelTalksFilm) August 24, 2026

OMG the concept of having to wait another week pic.twitter.com/yOcGKss712

— stuff (@stuffiseeonline) August 24, 2026

Still, it's easy to see why fans might be excited for such a relatively small development. The last time we saw a live-action Hal Jordan wearing the mask was when Ryan Reynolds played the character for his 2011 standalone movie, and we all know how that went.

As the DCU comes together, moments like these can be just as important as the projects themselves. Fans clamored for a first look at Robert Pattinson as Batman and again flocked to see him throw on the cowl for The Batman Part 2. David Corenswet's Superman drew eyes when his costume was revealed back in 2024.

As Hal Jordan seemingly winds down his time as a Green Lantern, we've yet to see what Pierre's John Stewart looks like in the suit. We'll hopefully get a better look when he reprises his role for the DCU's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, next year.

While we wait for Lanterns Episode 3 this weekend, August 30, you can see what IGN thought of Episode 2. You can also learn about the villain some viewers think is hiding in plain sight, as well as what DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn had to say about the gritty tone for the new DCU series.

items.title: Vampire Hunter D Returns: The Cult-Classic Horror Series Finds New Life in 2026
items.description: With a new Western comic book series in the works and a theatrical rerelease slated for 2027, the Vampire Hunter D franchise is suddenly back in the spotlight.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Vampire Hunter D is a franchise that has enjoyed a long, healthy lifespan as a series of Japanese light novels, but has never really been explored to its fullest in other media. The last Vampire Hunter D film to be released was 2001's Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust. Luckily for fans of the wandering hero known only as D, there's been some new momentum surrounding the franchise recently, including both a brand-new Western comics series and a theatrical rerelease.

First up, Dark Horse Comics is releasing a new miniseries called Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood. The series isn't an adaptation of one of Hideyuki Kikuchi's novels, but is rather an original story set in that post-apocalyptic universe. Fortress of Blood is written by Chris Condon (That Texas Blood) and illustrated by Filipe Andrade (The Many Deaths of Laila Starr).

The creative team also includes colorist Jordie Bellaire and letterer Frank Cvetkovic. Andrade illustrated the main cover for issue #1, with variants by Riccardo Federici and Yoshitaka Amano. Here's Dark Horse's official summary of the first issue:

The first official comic series based on Hideyuki Kikuchi’s Vampire Hunter D! A vampire lord has marshalled his forces and is marching on human settlements aiming to leave no survivors! One thing stands among his path to the next city—the old fortress. There, a family of outcasts will need to buy enough time for the humans to flee. And wandering this same path is the beautiful, indomitable hunter—half-human, half-vampire—known as D.

Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood #1 will be released on December 16. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.

On the film front, GKIDS revealed that Bloodlust is getting a theatrical rerelease in 2027, just after the film's 25th anniversary.

GKIDS is proud to announce the acquisition of North American rights to VAMPIRE HUNTER D: BLOODLUST. 🩸

The rarely-screened gothic horror classic from Yoshiaki Kawajiri and MADHOUSE will get a full theatrical release in 2027.

More details soon!https://t.co/UAi0WXpGqN pic.twitter.com/jTfCJ7qDWl

— GKIDS Films (@GKIDSfilms) August 22, 2026

There are no further details regarding a release date or possible 4k Blu-ray release, but hopefully Bloodlust returning to theaters will spark new interest in the series and pave the way for another film or anime series. Previously, an anime called Vampire Hunter D: Resurrection was announced in 2015, but work on the series seemingly stalled out during the COVID-19 pandemic.

For more on this cult-favorite franchise, check out IGN's Hidden Treasures retrospective on Vampire Hunter D.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

items.title: Anirudh Pisharody Says He's 'So Down' to Play Nightcrawler in Marvel's X-Men Movie
items.description: 9-1-1’s Anirudh Pisharody is ready to take on the role of Nightcrawler for Marvel Studio’s upcoming X-Men reboot, and fans are rallying behind him.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
9-1-1’s Anirudh Pisharody is ready to take on the role of Nightcrawler for Marvel Studio’s upcoming X-Men reboot, and fans are rallying behind him.

The cast of Marvel’s X-Men flick is still being fleshed out, leaving ample room for speculation as to who will be joining the already-confirmed list of stars. A few were confirmed at D23 this year, with Inde Navarrette revealed as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, and Adam Driver as Mister Sinister.

There are a few notable mutants who have yet to be revealed as part of the film, one of whom is Nightcrawler. While Alan Cumming reprising the role in Avengers: Doomsday, Marvel’s X-Men movie is expected to be a reboot of the franchise, meaning that a different, younger actor could be stepping into the role moving forward.

Enter Anirudh Pisharody. He’s an Indian-American actor best known for his performances in Never Have I Ever and 9-1-1, with other notable roles in Big Sky, The Goldbergs, Last Man Standing, and Unit 234.

On August 23, Pisharody responded to a fan’s tweet showing a side-by-side of the actor and panels of Nightcrawler from the X-Men comics. “Anirudh would devour as Nightcrawler,” they wrote.

“So, so down,” Pisharody responded in a quote tweet, tagging Marvel Studios alongside the scheming devil face emoji.

so so down @MarvelStudios 😈 https://t.co/OAPM6lvOYP

— Anirudh Pisharody (@AnirudhPish) August 23, 2026

Fans are flooding the comments section to vouch for him, with multiple users tagging Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige on several different platforms to make sure he’s aware of just how eager they are to see him in the role. (Still others are holding out hope that he'll take the role of Prince Naveen in Disney's upcoming live action Princess and the Frog remake.)

“Yes, make your move!” one excited fan wrote.

“I would be down if you could master a German accent,” another remarked.

“Role assigned to you already,” another wrote. “Remember me when it happens…”

Pisharody isn’t the only notable name vying for a role in Marvel’s X-Men movie; in a similar story, Reacher star Agnez Mo also responded to fan calls for Feige to cast her as Psylocke on social media.

“Thanks! I’m just gonna put it out to the universe… Psylocke,” she wrote, tagging the Marvel and Marvel Studios accounts.

Other names already confirmed for Marvel’s X-Men include Samara Weaving as Emma Frost (one of the most accurate castings we’ve seen thus far, to be frank), and Kit Connor as Cyclops.

Thanks! I’m just gonna put it out to the universe… Psylocke. @MarvelStudios @Marvel 💜

(Although @BoinkBuzz that’s my AI pic tho 😫) https://t.co/Lb5oCFEnhk

— AGNEZ MO (@agnezmo) August 23, 2026

With Avengers: Doomsday looming on the horizon, it’s expected that more will be revealed about the new generation of X-Men in the coming months. For more on the project, you can check out what Sadie Sink had to say about her ‘mysterious’ role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day and how she feels now that her big secret is out in the open.

Image Credits: Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images, Marvel

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Adds New Dynamic Cosmetic Options for Certain Characters Like Ghost
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is adding more options for how your operators appear in-game.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is adding more options for how your operators appear in-game.

The recently released Modern Warfare 4 beta has given players their first look at a ton of features, maps, and other content that will be available in the final game. Some of these things were heavily advertised before launch, such as the fluidity of movement and a new system that randomly generates gun builds for you.

One feature that was kept under wraps, however, allows players to equip different cosmetic items on the fly in-game. Ghost, for instance, can remove his mask (which comically reveals another cloth mask underneath) and put it back on. Valeria can equip a hockey mask. And Captain Price can smoke a cigar, which will appear on-screen in first-person at all times unless you take it out.

You Can Remove Ghost's Mask in Modern Warfare 4 using the NEW 'Operator Variant' Feature in the Emote Wheel: pic.twitter.com/ABJma6tvsy

— DETONATED (@DETONATEDcom) August 23, 2026

this is the best MW4 mastercraft the cigar actually stays in ur mouth until you respawn lol pic.twitter.com/sFWQUrV02k

— B23 (@B23COD) August 21, 2026

It's a fun touch and one that will almost certainly be taken advantage of in premium skins. As of right now, we're not sure what skins to expect in MW4, but Call of Duty has promised to keep things more grounded after fan backlash to previous games. Specifically, they said there will be "no Lady Gaga. No Omni-Man. No Teletubbies. No SpongeBob."

The fan reception on Modern Warfare 4's beta has been fairly divisive so far. Some fear that the game is a bit too fast, especially for having relatively small maps. The time-to-kill is extremely rapid, but Infinity Ward has addressed much of this feedback from fans so far. The studio has released patches for the beta addressing TTK, spawns, and is also looking to make improvements to the gunsmith system for launch.

IGN spoke with some of MW4's multiplayer leads last week ahead of the beta, and they made it clear this playtest is essential in helping shape the final game. "To me, this beta feels like the start of the conversation with the public, you know what I mean? We're excited to basically put that out there and we'll see what happens next. We want to just keep talking and keep learning and trying to find out what we can do better," said Jackie Reynolds, Modern Warfare 4's multiplayer design lead.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Pokémon Collector Poses as Buyer to Recover $4,000 Worth of Stolen Cards in 'Vigilante' Sting Operation
items.description: Canadian collector Emilio Kihien took matters into his own hands after police said they “couldn’t do much” to help him recover $4,000 worth of stolen Pokemon cards.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Canadian collector Emilio Kihien took matters into his own hands after police said they “couldn’t do much” to help him recover $4,000 worth of stolen Pokémon cards.

Kihien was conducting what he thought was a standard sale for a few highly-graded, officially-encapsulated Pokémon trading cards at his home in Coquitlam when the buyers handed him $4,000 in phony bills, snatched the goods, and ran. Kihien gave chase, even hanging onto the side of the thieves’ getaway car before falling onto the road, suffering bruising and a painful bout of road rash as a result.

His next step was to contact police — but he says authorities told him they “couldn’t do much” to help him recover his stolen property. According to Kihien, one officer even told him it’d be better to try and catch the culprits himself.

“The police response — they really didn’t seem like they were gonna help me that much. One of the officers literally said, ‘If it was me, I’d probably just try to set them up myself,’" he told local outlet CTV News.

A few days later, one of Kihien’s buddies came across a listing for the stolen cards online. The thieves even used the exact same images Kihien had included in his original posting.

items.title: Kit Harington Takes Over as Gilderoy Lockhart After Nicholas Hoult Exits HBO's Harry Potter Season 2
items.description: Game of Thrones alum Kit Harington has reportedly stepped in to fill the role of Gilderoy Lockhart in Harry Potter Season 2, replacing Nicholas Hoult in a surprise recasting decision for the HBO show.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Game of Thrones alum Kit Harington has reportedly stepped in to fill the role of Gilderoy Lockhart in Harry Potter Season 2, replacing Nicholas Hoult in a surprise recasting decision for the HBO show.

The Jon Snow actor officially filled the role following the news that Hoult had taken the part of the Defense Against the Dark Arts professor earlier this month, according to Deadline. Scheduling issues are said to be the cause of his exit, as HBO struggled to work around two of his pre-existing projects when the shooting schedule was changed.

When it was determined Hoult would no longer be able to join the Hogwarts staff, HBO dug through its history with the Game of Thrones cast to pick up Harington instead. It's unclear if the Harry Potter show's second season will change with the recast, though Deadline reported that the actor behind Westeros' defender in the North is already excited to play Gilderoy Lockhart.

Harington is best known for his work on Game of Thrones, but he also appeared as Dane Whitman in Marvel's Eternals, Henry Muck in Industry, and Salen Kotch in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. Although it might be a surprise to see him take over for Hoult in Harry Potter Season 2, Hogwarts — and even the part he will play — aren't uncharted territory for the actor.

He was one of the many A-listers to lend their voice to Audible's Full-Cast Audio Editions for the Harry Potter book series last year. While the project featured Keira Knightley as Professor Umbridge and James McAvoy as Mad-Eye Moody, Harington played Gilderoy Lockhart. His work must have made a good enough impression with those at HBO, as he's now set to reprise the role in live-action for Season 2.

"I read it, and like so many generations, I was entranced, and then I was a huge fan all through my teenage years," Harington told Audible, as shared by Deadline. "I think there’s a little bit of Gilderoy Lockhart in all of us," he added.

Gilderoy Lockhart first made his live-action debut in 2002's Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. Alongside the then-leading trio of Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, and Emma Watson, he was portrayed by Kenneth Branagh.

HBO renewed Harry Potter for Season 2 in May, with reports at the time suggesting filming was scheduled to begin this fall. Season 1, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, is set to transport viewers to a TV series take on Harry (Dominic McLaughlin), Ron (Alastair Stout), and Hermione's (Arabella Stanton) story this Christmas.

items.title: ESPN Unlimited Is Celebrating Its First Anniversary With a Price Hike
items.description: ESPN Unlimited and ESPN Select are getting price hikes next month, making one Disney+ bundle more valuable than ever.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
According to a support page on ESPN’s website, both ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited are getting price hikes.

Starting September 17, ESPN Unlimited plans will be increasing by $2, while ESPN Select plans get a smaller $1 hike. The ESPN increases will also affect the price of the existing Disney+ bundle with ESPN Select, though ESPN Unlimited bundles will seemingly retain the same monthly pricing.

ESPN Price Hike Taking Effect September 17

  • ESPN Select:
    • Monthly: Increasing to $13.99/month from $12.99/month
    • Annual: Increasing to $139.99 from $129.99
  • ESPN Unlimited:
    • Monthly: Increasing to $31.99/month from $29.99/month
    • Annual: Increasing to $319.99 from $299.99
  • Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select:
    • Basic: Increasing to $21.99/month from $19.99/month
    • Premium: Increasing to $32.99/month from $19.99/month
  • Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Unlimited:
    • Basic: Staying at $35.99/month
    • Premium: Staying $44.99/month

ESPN Unlimited first launched almost exactly a year ago, in August 2025. The service was pitched as a particularly inclusive sports streaming service in an otherwise complicated landscape of divided licenses and leagues. ESPN Select launched at the same time to functionally replace ESPN+, with existing subscribers automatically moved over to the new plan.

ESPN has admittedly grown its content offerings since that initial launch. MLB.tv was moved to the ESPN app starting with the 2026 season, and a sublicensing deal with The CW expanded the service’s roster of college sports. More recently, ESPN acquired NFL media assets, and the NFL Network just became available to Unlimited plan subscribers on July 30.

Disney+ increased its own prices by a similar $2 margin last October. For its standalone plans, ESPN is following a similar approach of announcing the hike several weeks before it goes into effect for both new and returning subscribers, giving potential “new” customers an extra incentive to sign up before then.

Unlike the standalone ESPN plans, the price increase on the Disney+ bundle with ESPN Select has already gone into effect for new subscribers. The fact that the price increase doesn’t seem to be touching the ESPN Unlimited bundles increases the “value” of those bundles, assuming subscribers would already be interested in all three services.

It’s also worth nothing that the price hike trend extends far beyond the Disney ecosystem. Paramount+ and Netflix both announced price hikes earlier this year, while Peacock just increased its own streaming plan prices for the fourth time in four years. Will there ever be an endpoint to the price hikes? Here’s to hoping.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
